module purpose: TWI (I2C) peripheral: it accepts bus requests (bus_req_i) to write/read control and FIFO data, stores control settings, runs a clock generator and a phase generator, drives a bit-level TWI engine that samples/produces SDA/SCL, presents FIFO read/write interfaces to instantiated FIFO subunits, reports status and responses on bus_rsp_o, exposes a clock-enable output clkgen_en_o and an interrupt irq_o.

use-case flows.value: control register settings (enable, prescaler index, clock divisor, clock-stretch enable) written by bus writes
enqueue a transmit command / data into the TX FIFO (wdata + write enable) from a bus write
clock generation (tick) and phase sequencing, and the TWI engine's bit-level transmit/receive operations that drive/observe SDA and SCL
readback of control and status fields and RX FIFO data returned on bus_rsp_o.data
interrupt event (irq_o) produced from ctrl.enable, fifo.tx_avail and engine.busy
what the block clears on rstn_i: bus response, control fields, clock generator counters, phase state, engine registers and I/O flip-flops

conceptual assets.concept: Control settings (enable, prescaler index, clock-divisor, clock-stretch enable) that configure clock generation and enable/disable the engine
conceptual assets.reasoning: These fields are written by bus writes in the bus_access process (assignments at lines 136--139). Map evidence: the bus request record fields source the registers (bus_req_i occurrence id 6 line 136 SOURCES -> ctrl.enable; occ.7 line 137 SOURCES -> ctrl.prsc; occ.8 line 138 SOURCES -> ctrl.cdiv; occ.9 line 139 SOURCES -> ctrl.clkstr). The values are held in registers (ctrl.enable occ.3 CLOCKED_BY -> clk_i; ctrl.prsc occ.3 CLOCKED_BY -> clk_i; ctrl.cdiv occ.3 CLOCKED_BY -> clk_i; ctrl.clkstr occ.2 CLOCKED_BY -> clk_i). The RTL uses those registers in clock_generator (clk tick selection uses ctrl.prsc and ctrl.cdiv at lines 257--261) and in the engine (engine.state(2) <= ctrl.enable at line 321) and in clk_gen.halt (line 296 uses ctrl.clkstr). Therefore the correct behavior of clocking, engine enable, and clk-stretching depends on the integrity of these stored settings (map records cited above allow checking which occurrence implements each role).

conceptual assets.concept: Clock-generation decision (clk_gen.tick and clk_gen.cnt) that sequences engine steps and FIFO transfers
conceptual assets.reasoning: clk_gen.tick is produced by the clock_generator process (compare cnt to ctrl.cdiv and select by ctrl.prsc and clkgen_i at lines 257--262) and gates engine and FIFO actions (clk_gen.tick appears in gating records for fifo.tx_re line 199 and engine.state progression line 329). Map evidence: clkgen_i at occurrence 2 (line 257) GATES clk_gen.cnt/clk_gen.tick; ctrl.prsc at occurrence 5 (line 257) SELECTS clk_gen.cnt/clk_gen.tick; ctrl.cdiv at occurrence 5 (line 258) CONSTRAINS clk_gen.cnt and clk_gen.tick; clk_gen.cnt occurrence 3 (line 254) and clk_gen.tick occurrence 6 (line 259) are CLOCKED_BY clk_i. Because engine progression and FIFO reads depend on the tick condition (map: clk_gen.tick GATES fifo.tx_re and GATES engine.state), the integrity and availability of the tick decision are established by the RTL.

conceptual assets.concept: TX FIFO transmit command/data (the command bytes written by the bus that the engine consumes to drive SDA/SCL)
conceptual assets.reasoning: A bus write (lines 197--199 and the tx_fifo_inst port map lines 172--195) provides the TX data and write-enable that the FIFO sub-unit receives; the engine later reads that FIFO entry into engine.sreg and uses it for bit transmission (engine.sreg <= fifo.tx_rdata at line 327). Map evidence: the bus request at occurrence id 14 (line 198) SOURCES fifo.tx_wdata; fifo.tx_wdata occurrence id 2 (line 188) CONNECTS into tx_fifo_inst.wdata_i; fifo.tx_we occurrence id 2 (line 189) CONNECTS into tx_fifo_inst.we_i; tx FIFO output fifo.tx_rdata occurrence id 2 (line 193) CONNECTS tx_fifo_inst.rdata_o and is later DERIVES_FROM into engine.sreg (engine.sreg occ.5 line 327 DERIVES_FROM fifo.tx_rdata). The RTL therefore establishes that the engine's transmitted payload equals the FIFO contents selected by these signals, so integrity of TX FIFO writes is established.

conceptual assets.concept: RX FIFO received data (bytes captured from SDA and written to the RX FIFO for bus readback)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Received bits are sampled into engine.sreg and, on completion, are written into the RX FIFO (fifo.rx_wdata <= engine.sreg(...) at line 228; fifo.rx_we <= engine.done at line 229), then the bus read returns rx_rdata on bus_rsp_o.data (line 156). Map evidence: engine.sreg occurrence id 2/5 (lines 228,327) SOURCES fifo.rx_wdata (fifo.rx_wdata occ.3 line 228 DERIVES_FROM engine.sreg) and engine.done occurrence id 2 (line 229) CARRIES -> fifo.rx_we (which connects to rx_fifo_inst.we_i at occurrence id 2 line 220). The bus response at bus_rsp_o occurrence id 16 (line 156) COPIES fifo.rx_rdata for the readback. The RTL thus establishes that bus reads retrieve the bytes the engine captured and wrote into the RX FIFO, so integrity of the received data path is established.

conceptual assets.concept: Engine sequencing state and bit counter (engine.state, engine.bitcnt) that control TWI protocol steps
conceptual assets.reasoning: The engine's finite-state and bit counter determine when SDA/SCL are driven, when bits are sampled, when engine.done is asserted, and when FIFO transfers occur (twi_engine process, lines 301--398). Map evidence: engine.state is held in a register (engine.state occ.3 line 321 CLOCKED_BY -> clk_i) and is selected in the case statements (map: engine.state SELECTS engine.bitcnt/engine.sreg at occurrence 4 line 322); engine.bitcnt is registered (engine.bitcnt occ.3 line 326 CLOCKED_BY -> clk_i) and gates done and SDA behavior (map: engine.bitcnt GATES engine.done and io_con.sda_out at occurrences cited). ctrl.enable is copied into engine.state(2) (map: ctrl.enable occ.10 line 321 CARRIES -> engine.state). Because many protocol outputs and FIFO interactions are conditional on engine.state and engine.bitcnt (map: multiple GATED_BY and SELECTED_BY records), the integrity of the engine state and counter is an established asset.

conceptual assets.concept: Physical TWI outputs (SDA and SCL) that leave the block (twi_sda_o, twi_scl_o) and the I/O-forwarding registers that drive them
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module drives the external pins from internal I/O control registers: twi_sda_o <= io_con.sda_out (line 406) and twi_scl_o <= io_con.scl_out (line 407). Map evidence: twi_sda_o occurrence 2 (line 406) COPIES io_con.sda_out; twi_scl_o occurrence 2 (line 407) COPIES io_con.scl_out. The internal io_con.sda_out and io_con.scl_out are clocked and selected by engine states/phases (io_con.sda_out occ.3 line 335 CLOCKED_BY clk_i; io_con.scl_out occ.4 line 341 CLOCKED_BY clk_i and many SELECTED_BY records). Because these outputs are the signals that implement the observable I2C waveform, the RTL establishes their integrity role: engine/phase decisions and stored io_con bits determine the external signal levels (map records and assignments cited above).

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt event reported on irq_o that signals 'ready-to-send' (ctrl.enable & not fifo.tx_avail & not engine.busy)
conceptual assets.reasoning: irq_o is produced in the irq_generator process (irq_o <= ctrl.enable and (not fifo.tx_avail) and (not engine.busy) at line 239). Map evidence: irq_o occurrence 3 (line 239) has a GATED_BY record with guard 'ctrl.enable and (not fifo.tx_avail) and (not engine.busy)' and CLOCKED_BY at that line (occurrence 3 CLOCKED_BY -> clk_i); ctrl.enable, fifo.tx_avail and engine.busy appear in the gate targets. Because irq_o is the reported event consumers rely on, the RTL explicitly establishes integrity of the interrupt relation (the port value follows the boolean expression on the cited lines and map records).
